newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Anglo American is considering restructuring its gold interests, which could result in one or more mergers of the existing Anglogold companies.

- Diesel prices were set to decline by up to twenty cents a litre in March , taking 0.4-0.6 of a percentage point off the annual consumer inflation rate, Transnet economist Mike Schussler said at the weekend.

- Computer company IBM SA reported a 27 percent slump in attributable income to 73.8 million rand for the year to end-December after the unsuccessful introduction of a low-end personal computer product ate into earnings.

- The Reserve Bank would retain its position as the market-maker in government bonds for at least another year to give the finance department time to implement essential structural changes to the bond market, a department spokesman said at the weekend.

- Mossgas, the troubled 12 billion rand synthetic fuel producer, has proposed in the feasibility studies of the petro chemical initiative that it be turned into a gas-based petrochemicals feedstock producer.
- Plans are afoot to move the reduction plant associated with JCI's hot briquetted iron project in Mozambique to Beira instead of the Zimbabwe border, the company said at the weekend.
- A huge inflow of foreign exchange in January pushed up the gross gold and foreign exchange reserves held by the Reserve Bank to 11.8 billion, the Bank said on Friday.
- People should not expect too much from the relaxation of exchange controls, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said.
- IBM of South Africa put a weak year behind it.
- The South African economy is expected to have a 2.29 percent growth in 1997 and the inflation rate should remain in single figures, according to economists.
- Gauteng's most wanted man escaped from custody after corrupt policemen signed fradulent release forms, it was revealed by police sources last night.
